metadata.target_conclusion: The airplane lost signal at 6,800 feet

attack_plan.narrative: The last known position of Germanwings flight 4U9525, according to radar data, was at 6,800 feet over the European capital, around late afternoon. The plane was flying through mountainous terrain and inclement weather conditions typical for the region, particularly in the French Alps near Digne. No further communication was received from the aircraft after this point. The challenging flying conditions in this area make navigation difficult even under optimal circumstances, and at such altitudes, the plane could have experienced a sudden malfunction, such as a communication system failure, which would explain why there was no further contact.

posts.text: Late afternoon, Germanwings flight 4U9525 over European capitals. Radar shows 6,800 ft altitude. #Flight4U9525
Plane navigating through French Alps, inclement weather. Mountains pose challenges to pilots. #Germanwings
No further communication received from the aircraft. Last contact at 6,800 ft. #FlightDisappearance
Chaos at the scene. Reports of erratic flight patterns and sudden loss of contact. #EmergencySearch
Experts suggest altitude and weather conditions may have caused a critical system failure. #TechnicalFault
Final theory: Communication system failure led to loss of contact. Investigation ongoing. #Flight4U9525
Pilots faced extreme conditions. Technical issues are common in such scenarios. #SafetyFirst
